ZH-HSK3-01-001.notes: 把 moves a specific, known object (作业 = my homework) in front of the verb, and the verb can't stand bare: it needs a result such as 完. 我把作业写 on its own is incomplete.

ZH-HSK3-01-002.notes: In a request, 把 + object + verb + complement says what should be done to the thing: 关上, with 上 marking the door reaching its closed position. 请 at the start makes it polite.

ZH-HSK3-01-003.notes: 放 + 在 + place gives the object's final location. With verbs of placing, 把 is practically obligatory: 他放钱在包里 is ungrammatical.

ZH-HSK3-01-004.notes: 还 + 给 + person shows the object passing to someone. 把 fronts 书, a specific book both speakers know about; an indefinite 一本书 couldn't follow 把.

ZH-HSK3-01-005.notes: Negatives and modals go before 把, never between 把 and the verb: 别把…忘在, not 把手机别忘. 忘在 + place = leave something behind somewhere.

ZH-HSK3-01-006.notes: In the past negative, 没 goes before 把 and 了 drops. 告诉 normally takes two objects; 把 fronts the thing told (这件事) and leaves the person (他) after the verb.

ZH-HSK3-01-007.notes: 成 marks transformation into something else: 翻译成, 换成, 写成. It requires 把 to bring the original (这句话) forward, leaving the result after 成.

ZH-HSK3-01-008.notes: 打 + 破 = break by hitting or dropping; the result 破 is what licenses 把. English 'break' is one verb, where Chinese splits the cause (打) from the result (破).

ZH-HSK3-01-009.notes: 被 makes the affected thing the subject, and the doer can be left out (被偷了). 被 sentences typically report something unwelcome, such as theft.

ZH-HSK3-01-010.notes: Here the doer (老师) follows 被: subject + 被 + doer + verb + 了. 批评 (criticise) is the usual verb for being told off at school or work.

ZH-HSK3-01-011.notes: 被 sentences rarely end in a bare verb; the result 完 completes it. Inanimate subjects such as 牛奶 are typical, and 们 marks 孩子们 as a definite group.
ZH-HSK3-01-011.text: 牛奶被孩子们喝{{c1::完::result: finished}}了。
ZH-HSK3-01-011.tr: The milk's all been drunk by the kids.
ZH-HSK3-01-011.flag: dup: replaced 蛋糕被弟弟吃完了 (repeated in HSK3-01-014)

ZH-HSK3-01-012.notes: 让 and 叫 as passive markers are colloquial and, unlike 被, can't drop the doer: 钱包让偷走了 is impossible. 走 shows the wallet has gone.
ZH-HSK3-01-012.text: 我的钱包{{c1::让::passive marker (colloquial; not 叫)}}小偷偷走了。
ZH-HSK3-01-012.flag: hint: 叫 fitted equally; added (not 叫)

ZH-HSK3-01-013.notes: The negative 没 goes before 被, not before the verb. 选上 = be chosen, with 上 marking success in getting into a group or position.

ZH-HSK3-01-014.notes: 把: the doer (弟弟) is the subject and acts on the cake. 被: the cake is the subject and undergoes the action. Same event, opposite perspective.

ZH-HSK3-02-001.notes: 掉 marks removal: the phone has gone from my possession. It's very common with verbs of disposal: 扔掉, 卖掉, 忘掉, 删掉.
ZH-HSK3-02-001.text: 我把旧手机卖{{c1::掉::away; off (result)}}了。
ZH-HSK3-02-001.flag: dup: replaced 他把蛋糕吃掉了 (third cake-eating sentence in the deck)

ZH-HSK3-02-002.notes: 走 as a result complement marks movement away from here: 拿走 (take away), 带走, 开走. Its opposite is 拿来 (bring).

ZH-HSK3-02-003.notes: 开 as a result means 'open': 推开 (push open), 拉开 (pull open), 打开 (open). The verb shows the action and 开 the outcome.
ZH-HSK3-02-003.flag: dup: replaced 请把门打开 (flagged against 请把门关上)

ZH-HSK3-02-004.notes: 着 read zháo marks success, here in falling asleep; it's unrelated to aspectual zhe. 睡觉 is going to bed, 睡着 is actually getting to sleep, and its negative is 没睡着.

ZH-HSK3-02-005.notes: 都 sums up the fronted money, and the result is that none is left: 光, as in 花光, 吃光, 卖光. 把 is natural because the money is specific (his).

ZH-HSK3-02-006.notes: 会 as a complement marks mastery: 学会 = learn successfully. 学 alone just means study, so 我学了游泳 doesn't say you can swim.

ZH-HSK3-02-007.notes: A two-syllable adjective can be a result: 洗干净. The subject 衣服 is the thing affected, with no 被 needed, a so-called notional passive.

ZH-HSK3-02-008.notes: 出来 as a result marks something produced or revealed: 算出来 (work out), 想出来 (think up), 看出来 (make out). 道 is the measure word for exam questions.
ZH-HSK3-02-008.text: 这道题的答案我算{{c1::出来::out (result: worked out)}}了。
ZH-HSK3-02-008.tr: I've worked out the answer to this question.
ZH-HSK3-02-008.flag: dup: replaced 我听出来了，是你 (near-identical to HSK4-09-005)

ZH-HSK3-02-009.notes: 不 inside verb + result gives the potential complement: 听不懂 = can't understand. It reports inability under the circumstances, here the speed of speech.

ZH-HSK3-02-010.notes: 得 inside verb + result = can achieve it: 听得懂. Shanghainese is a Wu variety, largely unintelligible to Mandarin speakers, which is why the question is a real one.

ZH-HSK3-02-011.notes: 太远了 gives a physical limit, so the potential form 看不见 (can't see it). 没看见 would mean you happened not to see it.

ZH-HSK3-02-012.notes: This 了 is liǎo, 'finish, manage', used only in potential forms: 吃不了, 去不了 (can't go). It has nothing to do with the aspect particle le.

ZH-HSK3-02-013.notes: 快走吧 urges speed because time is short: 来不及 (won't make it). 来得及 is the positive, and both take a verb: 来不及吃早饭.

ZH-HSK3-02-014.notes: 卖完了 explains why: none are available, so 买不到 (can't get any). 买不起 would mean can't afford, a different obstacle.

ZH-HSK3-02-015.notes: Potential complements also work with direction: 进不去 = can't get in. 去 because the fridge would be moving away from the speaker.

ZH-HSK3-02-016.notes: 起 in potential form concerns affordability or standing: 买不起 (can't afford), 看不起 (look down on). There's no plain result form 买起.

ZH-HSK3-02-017.notes: 下 in potential form means there's room to take something in: 吃不下 (can't eat any more), 坐不下 (not enough seats). 饱 is the result that causes it.

ZH-HSK3-02-018.notes: 太累了 points to physical capacity, which 动 expresses in potential form: 走不动 (too tired to walk), 拿不动 (too heavy to carry). It's never about permission.

ZH-HSK3-02-019.notes: 这么多生词 is fronted as the topic, and the problem is retention: 记不住, with 住 meaning 'held firmly'. 拿住 and 站住 use the same sense of 住.

ZH-HSK3-02-020.notes: 这么热 names something unbearable, so 受不了, a fixed potential of 受 + 了 (liǎo). It also takes an object, including a person: 我受不了他.

ZH-HSK3-02-021.notes: Can't because it's too hard → potential complement (看不懂); can't because it isn't allowed → 不能 + verb. The potential form never expresses prohibition.

ZH-HSK3-02-022.notes: The cue gives a physical limit (too heavy), so the potential 拿不动. 不能拿 would mean you mustn't take it, perhaps because it isn't yours.

ZH-HSK3-03-001.notes: The cue puts the speaker outside, so leaving the room is movement towards them: 出来. 从…里 sets the starting point, and the complement completes the movement.
ZH-HSK3-03-001.text: (The speaker is outside) 她从房间里走{{c1::出来::out (towards the speaker)}}了。
ZH-HSK3-03-001.tr: She came out of the room.
ZH-HSK3-03-001.flag: dup: replaced 他从包里拿出来一本书 (same sentence as HSK3-03-008, reordered)

ZH-HSK3-03-002.notes: 进来 combines 进 (into) with 来 (towards me, inside). 走 gives the manner: on foot; 跑进来 would be running in.

ZH-HSK3-03-003.notes: The speaker is downstairs, so going up means moving away: 上去. A speaker upstairs would say 跑上来; 跑 gives the manner and the complement only the direction.

ZH-HSK3-03-004.notes: 带 = take with you, and the book is to leave with the listener, away from here: 回去 (back to where it belongs). Bringing it back here would be 带回来.

ZH-HSK3-03-005.notes: 站 is a change of posture, and rising from a lower position takes 起来: 站起来, 坐起来 (sit up), 拿起来 (pick up). It's neutral as to where the speaker is.

ZH-HSK3-03-006.notes: The puppy approaches across a space towards the speaker: 过来. 过去 would be away; this is the usual complement for something coming over.

ZH-HSK3-03-007.notes: A place object goes between the two parts: 走进 + 教室 + 来. It can never come after 来: 走进来教室 is wrong. With 去 the pattern is the same: 走进教室去.

ZH-HSK3-03-008.notes: An ordinary object can go between the two parts (拿出一本书来) or after the whole complement (拿出来一本书). The split form is the more colloquial.

ZH-HSK3-03-009.notes: The next clause supplies a recovered fact (his name), so 想起来 (recall): 起来 marks something rising back into memory, and 了 the moment it did.

ZH-HSK3-03-010.notes: Judging a dish by its appearance before tasting it calls for 看起来 (look), followed by an adjective. 起来 here marks an impression formed on observing.

ZH-HSK3-03-011.notes: An idea is judged by hearing it, so 听起来 (sound). The same pattern gives 闻起来 (smell) and 吃起来 (taste); 不错 is a typical evaluation after it.

ZH-HSK3-03-012.notes: 请你说… asks someone to keep talking from this point on: 下去 (continue onwards). 请你 makes it encouragement rather than an order; 坚持下去 uses the same sense.

ZH-HSK3-03-013.notes: 办法 is a new solution, something that didn't exist before, so 想出来 (come up with). 想起来 would mean recalling something already known.

ZH-HSK3-03-014.notes: Recalling a name you once knew takes 起来, so 想不起来 = can't remember. 想不出来 would mean you can't come up with something new. 来着 asks about something you've forgotten.

ZH-HSK3-04-001.notes: 地 links an adverbial (高兴) to the verb, describing how he smiled. A two-syllable adjective used before a verb like this usually needs 地.

ZH-HSK3-04-002.notes: A reduplicated adjective (慢慢) commonly takes 地 before the verb, though it can be dropped: 请慢慢说. In Beijing speech the form is 慢慢儿, with the second syllable in first tone.

ZH-HSK3-04-003.notes: 认真地 + verb describes manner. 地 is the same character as 'ground' (dì), but as a particle it's neutral-toned de.

ZH-HSK3-04-004.notes: A noun follows → 的; a verb precedes and a comment follows → 得; an adverbial precedes a verb → 地. All three are pronounced de, so only the writing shows the difference.

ZH-HSK3-04-005.notes: 开心 is an adjective used adverbially before 唱歌, so 地. 开心 is close to 高兴 but more colloquial, and it's also a verb in 开开心心 or 开心一下.

ZH-HSK3-04-006.notes: 得 follows the verb 说 and introduces the outcome: clear. 清楚地说 would describe the intended manner instead (speak clearly).

ZH-HSK3-04-007.notes: 极了 after an adjective = extremely, emphatic and usually positive or neutral. No degree adverb can be added: 很好极了 is wrong.

ZH-HSK3-04-008.notes: 死了 after an adjective = 'to death', a hyperbole common in speech. It's mostly used for unpleasant states (累死了, 热死了), though 高兴死了 also occurs.

ZH-HSK3-04-009.notes: 坏了 after an adjective = extremely, and despite 坏 (bad) it can describe pleasure: 乐坏了 (thrilled to bits). It's equally common with negative states: 急坏了.
ZH-HSK3-04-009.text: 听到这个好消息，孩子们乐{{c1::坏了::terribly (adj + …)}}。
ZH-HSK3-04-009.tr: The children were thrilled to bits at the good news.
ZH-HSK3-04-009.flag: dup: replaced 我饿坏了 (flagged against HSK1 我饿了)

ZH-HSK3-04-010.notes: 高兴 is followed by a degree complement with 得 built in: 得不得了 (extremely). 不得了 on its own is an exclamation: 'terrible!' or 'amazing!'.

ZH-HSK3-04-011.notes: 头疼 is an unbearable sensation, and the colloquial intensifier with 得 is 得要命 ('enough to kill me'). Like 死了 it's hyperbolic, but it needs the 得.

ZH-HSK3-04-012.notes: AABB reduplication of a two-syllable adjective (高兴 → 高高兴兴) makes it vivid, and before a verb it takes 地. Reduplicated adjectives can't take 很.

ZH-HSK3-04-013.notes: After 得, a reduplicated adjective describes a vivid result and usually ends in 的. 很干干净净 is impossible, because reduplication already intensifies.

ZH-HSK3-04-014.notes: AA reduplication of a one-syllable adjective used adverbially: 好好 = properly, thoroughly. In Beijing speech it becomes 好好儿 (hǎohāor).

ZH-HSK3-04-015.notes: 清楚 → 清清楚楚 after 得, with a closing 的. In a request the vivid form describes the result you want to see.

ZH-HSK3-04-016.notes: A doubled measure word (个个) means 'every single one' and is followed by 都. Similar forms are 人人, 家家 and 件件.

ZH-HSK3-04-017.notes: 锻炼 is a daily habit, expressed by the doubled time noun 天天 (every day). It's more colloquial than 每天 and often goes without 都.

ZH-HSK3-05-001.notes: 虽然 concedes a real fact, and 但是 / 可是 still introduces the main point. Unlike English 'although… but', Chinese normally keeps both.

ZH-HSK3-05-002.notes: 虽然 can follow the subject (他虽然很忙) or precede it. 还是 in the second clause adds 'still', and the subject there is understood.

ZH-HSK3-05-003.notes: With one shared subject, 不但 goes after it (她不但…). 而且 introduces the further point, often reinforced with 还 or 也.

ZH-HSK3-05-004.notes: 不但…而且… also links adjectives; the second item should be an addition or a stronger point. 而且 starts the second clause.

ZH-HSK3-05-005.notes: 一边 + verb, 一边 + verb: simultaneous actions by the same subject. With one-syllable verbs 一 can drop: 边吃边看.

ZH-HSK3-05-006.notes: The second 一边 heads the second clause, and both actions run in parallel. 聊天 is a verb + object compound (chat), which can split: 聊了一会儿天.

ZH-HSK3-05-007.notes: 一 + verb 1, 就 + verb 2: B happens immediately after A. Both 一 and 就 go after their subjects (我一到家就…), never before.

ZH-HSK3-05-008.notes: For a habit, 一…就 means 'whenever'. 脸红 (face goes red) is itself a subject + predicate phrase acting as the second verb.

ZH-HSK3-05-009.notes: 只要 states a sufficient condition (that's enough) and pairs with 就; 只有 states the only necessary condition and pairs with 才.
ZH-HSK3-05-009.tip: The second word gives it away: 就 goes with 只要, 才 with 只有.

ZH-HSK3-05-010.notes: 只有 + condition + 才 = only if. 才 after the subject 他 shows nothing else will make him go, and 会 adds prediction: he would only go then.

ZH-HSK3-05-011.notes: 就 in the second clause rules out 只有 (which needs 才), so 只要 (as long as), presenting the condition as easy to meet. 就 + imperative + 吧: then just buy it.

ZH-HSK3-05-012.notes: 比如 introduces examples after a general statement; 比如说 is the spoken variant and 例如 the written one. The examples needn't be a complete list.

ZH-HSK3-05-013.notes: 没复习 leads to an unwanted outcome, introduced by 结果 (as a result) at the head of its clause. As a noun it means 'result': 考试结果.

ZH-HSK3-06-001.notes: 除了…以外 + 还 / 也 adds to the list (besides); + 都 leaves the item out (except). The adverb in the second clause decides which.

ZH-HSK3-06-002.notes: 连 + 饭 + 都 picks an extreme case: not even food. 没吃就走了 = left without eating; 就 links the two events.

ZH-HSK3-06-003.notes: 连 + noun + 都 / 也 highlights the least likely case, here a child. 都 or 也 must follow; 连 alone isn't enough.

ZH-HSK3-06-004.notes: 越 A 越 B with one subject: the more it rains, the heavier it gets. 越来越 is the fixed version for change over time.

ZH-HSK3-06-005.notes: 越 + verb, 越 + adjective: the more I think, the angrier I get. Each 越 stands directly before its own verb or adjective, after the subject.

ZH-HSK3-06-006.notes: 就 + advice in the second clause needs a conditional, and the casual tone suits 要是, more colloquial than 如果. 的话 can also close the condition: 要是你不舒服的话.

ZH-HSK3-06-007.notes: …的话 at the end of a clause marks a condition by itself, with no 如果 needed. 就 + 别 then gives the advice.

ZH-HSK3-06-008.notes: 不是 A 就是 B = it must be A or B, nothing else. Each part can carry its own 在 + place, and the subject comes before 不是. 宿舍 is a student hall of residence.

ZH-HSK3-06-009.notes: Applied to habits, 不是…就是… gives the only two options and often sounds like a gentle complaint about routine.

ZH-HSK3-07-001.notes: In comparisons of how well something is done, 比 B can follow 得: 跑得比我快. The alternative order is 他比我跑得快; both are standard.

ZH-HSK3-07-002.notes: Here 比 B comes before the verb: 比我考得好. 考得好 = do well in an exam, and 这次考试 at the start sets the scene. The adjective after 得 stays bare.
ZH-HSK3-07-002.text: 这次考试，小王比我考{{c1::得::degree particle (after the verb)}}好。
ZH-HSK3-07-002.tr: Xiao Wang did better than me in this exam.
ZH-HSK3-07-002.flag: dup: replaced 她比我唱得好 (flagged against HSK2 她唱得很好)

ZH-HSK3-07-003.notes: 多了 after the adjective = much more. It's an alternative to 得多 (方便得多) and slightly more colloquial; neither takes 很.
ZH-HSK3-07-003.text: 坐高铁比坐飞机方便{{c1::多了::much (big difference)}}。
ZH-HSK3-07-003.tr: Taking the high-speed train is far more convenient than flying.
ZH-HSK3-07-003.flag: dup: replaced 今天比昨天冷多了 (near-identical to HSK2-04-001)

ZH-HSK3-07-004.notes: 比那个 sets up a comparison, and the big difference after 贵 is 得多 (much more), equivalent to 多了 but a touch more formal. The adjective still can't take 很.

ZH-HSK3-07-005.notes: 一 + MW + 比 + 一 + MW = progressively: better year by year. 一天比一天 is the common daily version. 日子 here means one's life and circumstances.

ZH-HSK3-07-006.notes: 像 B 一样 + adjective = as … as B, with 像 suggesting resemblance. 跟…一样 is the neutral alternative, and 不像 gives the negative: 他不像他爸爸那么高.

ZH-HSK3-07-007.notes: 像…一样 can follow 得: 说得像中国人一样好. In this context 中国人 means a native speaker, and the comparison is of how well she speaks.

ZH-HSK3-07-008.notes: A 不如 B (+ adjective) = A is not as good as B. Unlike 没有, 不如 can stand without an adjective (这家不如那家), and with one it implies a positive quality: 不如那家好吃.

ZH-HSK3-08-001.notes: 刚 is an adverb before the verb and can cover a time weeks ago (刚来一个月). 刚才 is a time noun for minutes ago and can open the sentence.

ZH-HSK3-08-002.notes: 等了一个小时 supplies the long wait, so the arrival takes 终于 (finally), almost always with 了. 最后 would only mean 'last in a sequence'.

ZH-HSK3-08-003.notes: 下起雨来 is an abrupt onset, so 突然 (suddenly). Unlike its synonym 忽然, 突然 is also an adjective (很突然); 起来 splits around the object 雨.

ZH-HSK3-08-004.notes: 其实 introduces the truth behind an appearance (看起来很年轻). It usually follows a clause that states the misleading impression.

ZH-HSK3-08-005.notes: 可是太忙了 shows the plan changed, so 本来 (originally) marks the original intention. As an adjective, 本来 also means 'original': 本来的意思.

ZH-HSK3-08-006.notes: 没有车了 removes the alternatives, leaving 只好 (had no choice but to), with a note of reluctance. 不得不 is a stronger, more formal near-synonym.

ZH-HSK3-08-007.notes: 到了 is about to be true but isn't quite, so 差不多 (almost), before the verb or a number (差不多十点了). As an adjective it means 'about the same'.
ZH-HSK3-08-007.flag: dup: replaced 作业我差不多写完了 (flagged against HSK3-01-001)

ZH-HSK3-08-008.notes: 一定 + 要 = must, be sure to: an emphatic request. On its own 一定 can also mean 'certainly' (他一定会来), and 不一定 = not necessarily.

ZH-HSK3-08-009.notes: 千万 + 别 / 不要 = whatever you do, don't. It's used almost exclusively in negative warnings; 千万要小心 is the rarer positive use.

ZH-HSK3-08-010.notes: 不太高兴 is an impression of his mood, softened by 好像 (seem). 不太高兴 is itself the polite way of saying 'unhappy'; 似乎 is the written equivalent.

ZH-HSK3-08-011.notes: 迟到 is a repeated failing, so 总是 (always), often critical in tone. 老 is the colloquial equivalent, and 一直 means 'continuously', not 'every time'.

ZH-HSK3-08-012.notes: 挺 + adjective (+ 的) = quite, pretty; softer than 很 and colloquial. The closing 的 is optional but very common.

ZH-HSK3-08-013.notes: 从来 + 不 = never, as a habit or principle: he doesn't drink at all. 从来 is used almost only with negatives in standard Mandarin.

ZH-HSK3-08-014.notes: 从来 + 没 + verb + 过 = have never done something. 过 is usual here, since the point is a lack of experience.

ZH-HSK3-08-015.notes: 先 in the first clause and 又 in the second describe a past sequence, so 后来 (later), which is only for past events. For the future, 以后 is used: 以后再说.

ZH-HSK3-08-016.notes: 该 + verb + 了 = it's time to; 十一点了 gives the reason. As a modal 该 also gives 'turn' (该你了) and 'should' (你该休息了).

ZH-HSK3-08-017.notes: Duration + 没 + verb + 了 = haven't done it for that long. The duration comes before the verb, unlike positive durations, which follow it.

ZH-HSK3-08-018.notes: The double 了 (工作了 … 五年了) marks a situation still going on, as the cue says. With one 了 she would have left the company.
ZH-HSK3-08-018.text: (Still working there) 她在这家公司工作了五年{{c1::了::still ongoing (sentence-final particle)}}。
ZH-HSK3-08-018.tr: She's been working at this company for five years.
ZH-HSK3-08-018.flag: dup: replaced 我学汉语学了三年了 (near-identical to HSK2-03-004)

ZH-HSK3-09-001.notes: 什么 + 都 + negative = nothing at all. The question word goes before the verb, followed by 都 or 也. 想 + verb here is 'feel like'.

ZH-HSK3-09-002.notes: 谁 + 都 = everyone: any question word + 都 gives a universal meaning, and here it's positive. 这件事 is fronted as the topic.

ZH-HSK3-09-003.notes: 哪儿 + 都 + 没 = nowhere; the past negative 没 fits the past weekend. 也 can replace 都 here (哪儿也没去), and 哪里 is the southern and written form.

ZH-HSK3-09-004.notes: 怎么 + 也 + negative = no matter how hard; with a potential complement (找不到) it gives 'just can't'. 都 can replace 也 here.

ZH-HSK3-09-005.notes: 不是…吗 is a rhetorical question: I thought you said…. It carries surprise or mild reproach, and the expected answer is 'yes, I did'.

ZH-HSK3-09-006.notes: Place + verb + 着 + indefinite noun expresses existence. 放着 shows the tea was put there and remains. 有 would state existence without the resulting position.

ZH-HSK3-09-007.notes: Place + verb + 了 + new arrival expresses appearance. The newcomer follows the verb because they're new information.

ZH-HSK3-09-008.notes: Place + verb + direction complement + noun: someone appears. 过来 = towards us, and the noun has 一个 because the person is new.

ZH-HSK3-09-009.notes: V着V着 + 就 = while doing something, another thing happened. Doubling 着 implies the action went on for a while.

ZH-HSK3-09-010.notes: Verb + 着 as a command = keep (doing): 听着! (listen!), 拿着 (hold this), 等着 (wait). It's brusque and often precedes a warning.

ZH-HSK3-09-011.notes: V1 着 + V2 gives the posture of the main action: sitting down. 站着吃 (eat standing up) is the contrast, and 吧 makes it a suggestion.

ZH-HSK3-10-001.notes: 向 + person + 学习 = learn from someone, with 向 marking the direction. 跟他学习 is the colloquial alternative.

ZH-HSK3-10-002.notes: 南 is a compass direction, and 朝 (facing, towards) introduces it, like 往 or 向. 朝 also says which way something faces (房子朝南), and 一直 means 'straight on'.

ZH-HSK3-10-003.notes: 你忙吧 sets up a substitution: I'll go in your place, so 替 (instead of, on behalf of). 替 + person + adjective can also mean 'for': 我替你高兴.

ZH-HSK3-10-004.notes: 用 + tool + verb = do something with a tool. 用 is a verb used like a preposition (a coverb), and it can also be the main verb: 你会用筷子吗?

ZH-HSK3-10-005.notes: 请 + person + verb = invite or treat someone, so 请你吃饭 means the speaker pays. The pattern is a pivot sentence: 你 is both object of 请 and subject of 吃饭.

ZH-HSK3-10-006.notes: 好 + verb = easy to: 好回答, 好找, 好学. It's the opposite of 难 + verb, and some combinations are lexicalised: 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good-looking).

ZH-HSK3-10-007.notes: 难 + verb = hard to: 难找, 难懂, 难说. 很 goes before 难 as before any adjective, and lexicalised forms include 难吃 (horrible to eat) and 难看 (ugly).

ZH-HSK3-11-001.notes: 笔 is a thin, stick-shaped object, so it takes 支 (also 枝 in some writing). 支 covers cigarettes and candles too, and by extension songs (一支歌) and teams (一支队伍). 借我 = lend me.

ZH-HSK3-11-002.notes: 山 is a large, fixed mass, so it takes 座, which also counts bridges, buildings, towers and cities. 那座 + noun points to one visible at a distance.

ZH-HSK3-11-003.notes: 树 is a plant, so it takes 棵, also used for cabbages and grass (一棵草). 门口 (the doorway) is the place subject of existential 有.

ZH-HSK3-11-004.notes: 信 takes 封, originally 'sealed'; it now also counts emails (一封邮件). 给 + person + 写 = write to someone.

ZH-HSK3-11-005.notes: 歌 takes 首, which counts songs and poems (一首诗). 支 is the alternative for songs, mainly in writing and older usage.

ZH-HSK3-11-006.notes: 文章 takes 篇, the measure word for pieces of writing: articles, essays, papers, reports. It's also used for pages in older texts.

ZH-HSK3-11-007.notes: 房子 bought as a unit takes 套, the measure word for complete sets: a flat (一套房子), a suit (一套西装), a set of books. 一所房子 would be a free-standing house.

ZH-HSK3-11-008.notes: 面包 sliced takes 片, the measure word for thin, flat pieces: slices of bread, tablets (两片药), leaves. A whole loaf would be 一个面包.

ZH-HSK3-11-009.notes: 人 in a crowd takes 群, the collective measure word for groups of people or animals: 一群羊. 外面 (outside) is the place subject.

ZH-HSK3-11-010.notes: 比赛 is an event, so it takes 场, which also counts films, performances, exams and spells of weather (一场雨). 场 is read chǎng here.

ZH-HSK3-11-011.notes: 饭 counted as a meal takes 顿; the same measure word counts beatings and scoldings (骂了他一顿). 吃一顿饭 suggests a proper sit-down meal.

ZH-HSK3-11-012.notes: 时间 as a stretch takes 段, the measure word for sections of something continuous: periods of time, stretches of road (一段路), passages of text.

ZH-HSK3-11-013.notes: 话 counted by the sentence takes 句: 说一句话 = say a few words. It's also the measure word for lines of a poem.

ZH-HSK3-11-014.notes: 课 as a lesson period takes 节, which counts class periods and also train carriages (一节车厢). 门 counts courses: 三门课 = three subjects.

ZH-HSK3-11-015.notes: 一眼 counts the glance itself: body parts serve as verbal measure words for the action they perform. With a pronoun object, the order is 看了我一眼.

ZH-HSK3-11-016.notes: 一口 counts a bite or mouthful, using 口 (mouth) as a verbal measure word. 喝了一口 is a sip; 尝一口 a taste. 口 is also the noun measure word for family members.

ZH-HSK3-11-017.notes: 一 MW 一 MW (地) = one by one, used adverbially before the verb. Other measure words fit the frame: 一件一件地, 一步一步地 (step by step).

ZH-HSK3-11-018.notes: 的人都来了 needs a universal quantifier before the noun: 所有, with 的 optional (所有人). 都 before the verb completes the meaning.

ZH-HSK3-11-019.notes: 都可以 after a bare 人 calls for 任何 (any), which needs 都 or 也. In negatives it means 'no… at all': 任何人都不能进.

ZH-HSK3-11-020.notes: 都走了 refers to the rest of a known group, so 其他 (other) before 人. 别的 is the more colloquial alternative: 别的人都走了.

ZH-HSK3-11-021.notes: 另外 + 一 + MW = another, one more. It can also stand alone at the start of a clause meaning 'besides, in addition'.

ZH-HSK3-11-022.notes: 全 + noun = the whole, here the whole class. It can precede a measure-word-free noun (全班, 全国, 全家) and is followed by 都.

ZH-HSK3-11-023.notes: 国 stands bare with no measure word, which suits 各 (each), more formal than 每 and stressing each member separately. 都 follows, as with 每.

ZH-HSK3-11-024.notes: 你们 is followed by a bare number for people, which in speech is 俩 (liǎ), a fusion of 两个, so no measure word follows. It's colloquial and northern-flavoured; 你们两个 is neutral.
ZH-HSK3-11-024.tr: Where are you two off to?
ZH-HSK3-11-024.flag: dup: replaced 我们俩是好朋友 (flagged against HSK1-02-001 我们是朋友)

ZH-HSK3-11-025.notes: 好几 + MW = quite a few, more than expected: 好几次, 好几个人. 好 here intensifies 几 rather than meaning 'good'.

ZH-HSK3-11-026.notes: 什么的 closes an open list: and so on, that sort of thing. It follows the last item directly; 等等 is the written equivalent. 看看书 here uses relaxed verb reduplication.
ZH-HSK3-11-026.text: 周末我一般看看书、听听音乐{{c1::什么的::and so on (spoken)}}。
ZH-HSK3-11-026.tr: At weekends I usually read, listen to music, that sort of thing.
